title: Half of Canada Is Sitting on Bare Rock #shorts
summary: The Canadian Shield covers about 5 million square kilometres, roughly half of Canada's land: bare rock, thin soil, muskeg and thousands of lakes.
sources: At 5 million km2, the Shield makes up roughly 50 per cent of Canada's land mass; bare rock, thin soils, muskeg; thousands of small lakes (The Canadian Encyclopedia, Canadian Shield, edited 11 Aug 2021): https://thecanadianencyclopedia.ca/en/article/shield

Two out of three people (66%) lived within 100 km of the southern Canada-US border, an area that represents about 4% of Canada's territory; 3.9 people per square km vs 35.3 in the US; a large land area (close to 9 million square km) (Statistics Canada, The Daily, 8 Feb 2017, 2016 Census): https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/n1/daily-quotidien/170208/dq170208a-eng.htm

scenes.narration: Half of Canada is sitting on bare rock.
The Canadian Shield: about {5 million|five million} square kilometres.
Thin soil, muskeg and thousands of small lakes. Tough place to farm.
So Canadians farmed and built just south of it, by the US border.
And the rock? Still there. Half of Canada.
